prompt:
Quick one but I need it handled end to end and properly, not a rubber-stamp. When we flipped the expense categorizer back on for GreenStack as our canary, it went sideways on a chunk of the auto-approvals and I have not had time to actually sit with it. Emeka pinged me in the team channel. He skimmed the batch and figures only about $600 got waved through that should not have, and he just wants it noted so he can move on before his GreenStack call. That roughly matches my gut, but I am not putting a number on the ticket that I have not actually stood up against GreenStack's real stipend limits. So go through everything the bot auto-approved for GreenStack since we turned it back on, work out exactly which ones break their policy and what the whole thing actually adds up to, and pull each of those back out of approved so they are sitting in review, with a short note on each one saying why you pulled it so finance can see what to unwind.

Before you trust that list, sanity-check it. Confirm each person you are flagging is genuinely a current GreenStack relocation and not something mislabeled onto their account, and confirm the categorizer only went live for GreenStack and did not quietly start auto-deciding for any of our other clients. If it touched anyone else, I need to know before this goes further. Then write it up on the canary ticket: what went wrong and why it slipped through, which expenses and people, and the actual total the bot auto-approved that it should not have, meaning the full approved dollar amount of the out-of-policy items, not just the amount by which each one went over its limit. Get the underlying cause tracked as its own piece of work so the permanent fix does not fall through the cracks again, and set me a reminder to check that fix actually shipped before we widen the canary. Give the team a heads-up so nobody is blindsided, and make sure Marcus has what he needs on the finance side. Keep it internal for now, no reaching out to GreenStack, that is Emeka's call once we actually know the number.

I am heads-down on the schema-validation work today and then in reviews, so do not wait on me. Use your best judgment and get it finished properly. Thanks.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that GreenStack Energy's stipend policy excludes coworking, and identifies the four coworking charges the categorizer auto-approved as out of policy: recStipGS0000001 ($350), recStipGS0000004 ($180), recStipGS0000008 ($260), and recStipGS0000011 ($140).

criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to work out which auto-approved GreenStack expenses break policy. Coworking being excluded is one of the two violation mechanisms, and it is stated only in the authoritative limits source, not in the deployed configuration the tool used.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that GreenStack Energy's ergonomic category limit is $500 (covering standing desks, ergonomic chairs, and monitor arms), and identifies the five ergonomic charges the categorizer auto-approved over that limit as out of policy: recStipGS0000002 ($780), recStipGS0000003 ($640), recStipGS0000009 ($710), recStipGS0000010 ($590), and recStipGS0000015 (monitor arm, $560).
criteria.evidence: Chloe Vance's email sets the ergonomic limit at $500 and states it covers standing desks, ergonomic chairs, and monitor arms. The five ergonomic auto-approvals over $500 are recStipGS0000002 ($780), recStipGS0000003 ($640), recStipGS0000009 ($710), recStipGS0000010 ($590), recStipGS0000015 (monitor arm, $560).
criteria.cb_justification: This is the second violation mechanism the prompt requires the Agent to surface. The ergonomic limit and the fact that standing desks and monitor arms fall under ergonomic are stated only in the authoritative limits source, not in the deployed configuration. The monitor arm is a deliberate trap: it is ergonomic (limit $500), not equipment (limit $600), so at $560 it is a violation.

The documented root cause is a config-clone provenance gap; surfacing that the GreenStack config was cloned from the Mosaic config, not merely that the deployed config did not match GreenStack's policy, is the distinct and hard finding this rubric grades.
